title: acs skill manifest (skills/<name>/acs.yaml)
description: What acs knows about one skill, declared beside it. Replaces the central workflows/phases.yaml registry: `phase` is the lifecycle group (the README table's order and the metrics grouping, nothing branches on it), `leg_of` names the entry point an internal leg serves, and `reads` / `writes` name the ARTIFACTS the skill consumes and produces. reads/writes are facts about the skill that hold in every workflow -- they are what `acs workflow validate` checks a step list's order against without any edge in the workflow file, and what the runtime input gate consults, so the two can never disagree about what a skill needs. A skill that declares neither reads nor writes is not a step candidate (setup, metrics, handoff and ship itself are skills, not steps). This file is acs's own: Claude Code's SKILL.md front matter is untouched by it.

phase.description: The lifecycle group, for ordering and grouping only. A leg omits it and reports its entry point's.

leg_of.description: The user-facing entry point this internal leg serves. A leg keeps its SKILL.md, agents, hooks and gate and stays Skill-invocable, but a workflow never names it -- the entry point dispatches to it. Mutually exclusive with reads/writes: a leg is not a step.

reads.description: The artifacts this skill consumes. `required` is what it cannot work without under a workflow; `optional` is what it uses when present and records the absence of when not. Standalone, a missing required read is a fallback rather than a refusal (§3.11).

artifactName.description: An artifact the pipeline passes between steps. `subject` is the run-level input (a ticket, a prompt or a document) and is written by no step.
